collection_schema.description: Disease-aware generic public-health collection schema generated for COVID-19 from structured task input and disease intelligence.

core_fields.name: disease
core_fields.description: Standard disease name for the requested task.

core_fields.name: virus_or_syndrome
core_fields.description: Specific pathogen, syndrome, or disease subtype if stated by the source.

core_fields.name: country
core_fields.description: Country where the human cases, deaths, outbreak, or surveillance data occurred.

core_fields.name: subnational_location
core_fields.description: State, province, city, county, district, hospital, or other subnational location as stated.

core_fields.name: date_reported
core_fields.description: Date when the data were reported or published; preserve partial dates when needed.

core_fields.name: event_start_date
core_fields.description: Start date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: event_end_date
core_fields.description: End date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: cases_confirmed
core_fields.description: Laboratory-confirmed or source-defined confirmed human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_probable
core_fields.description: Source-defined probable human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_suspected
core_fields.description: Source-defined suspected human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_unspecified
core_fields.description: Human cases where confirmation status is not clearly stated.

core_fields.name: deaths
core_fields.description: Deaths attributed to the reported disease event or surveillance period.

core_fields.name: case_definition
core_fields.description: Case definition or count label used by the source.

core_fields.name: source_id
core_fields.description: Workflow source identifier when available.

core_fields.name: source_url
core_fields.description: URL of the source from which the record was extracted.

core_fields.name: source_type
core_fields.description: Source category used by the data collection workflow.

core_fields.name: evidence_quote
core_fields.description: Verbatim source text supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: supporting_chunk_id
core_fields.description: Evidence chunk identifier supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: statistical_count_type
core_fields.description: Count semantics such as cumulative, annual, newly_reported, or point-in-time.

core_fields.name: reporting_period
core_fields.description: Reporting period or temporal aggregation window stated by the source.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about COVID-19.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify primary official reporting sources for COVID-19 human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in New York (state and city) during 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: NYSDOH and NYC DOHMH are the authoritative subnational agencies publishing weekly COVID-19 surveillance data for New York. Their dashboards, weekly reports, and data downloads are the highest-priority extractable collection sources for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC state-level COVID-19 surveillance data covering New York for the week of 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07.

count_semantics_notes: Separate cases, deaths, hospitalizations, test positivity, and wastewater signals — do not aggregate across metric types.

Distinguish between new/incident counts and cumulative totals; prefer incident counts for the 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07 window.

Test positivity rate is a surveillance signal, not a case count — do not substitute for cases_confirmed.
Wastewater surveillance data is a proxy signal — record separately and do not conflate with clinical case counts.

Cumulative counts must not be reported as incident counts for the target week.

Probable and suspected case definitions vary by jurisdiction and reporting period; record case classification as reported.

collection_schema.description: Disease-aware generic public-health collection schema generated for COVID-19 from structured task input and disease intelligence.

core_fields.name: disease
core_fields.description: Standard disease name for the requested task.

core_fields.name: virus_or_syndrome
core_fields.description: Specific pathogen, syndrome, or disease subtype if stated by the source.

core_fields.name: country
core_fields.description: Country where the human cases, deaths, outbreak, or surveillance data occurred.

core_fields.name: subnational_location
core_fields.description: State, province, city, county, district, hospital, or other subnational location as stated.

core_fields.name: date_reported
core_fields.description: Date when the data were reported or published; preserve partial dates when needed.

core_fields.name: event_start_date
core_fields.description: Start date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: event_end_date
core_fields.description: End date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: cases_confirmed
core_fields.description: Laboratory-confirmed or source-defined confirmed human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_probable
core_fields.description: Source-defined probable human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_suspected
core_fields.description: Source-defined suspected human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_unspecified
core_fields.description: Human cases where confirmation status is not clearly stated.

core_fields.name: deaths
core_fields.description: Deaths attributed to the reported disease event or surveillance period.

core_fields.name: case_definition
core_fields.description: Case definition or count label used by the source.

core_fields.name: source_id
core_fields.description: Workflow source identifier when available.

core_fields.name: source_url
core_fields.description: URL of the source from which the record was extracted.

core_fields.name: source_type
core_fields.description: Source category used by the data collection workflow.

core_fields.name: evidence_quote
core_fields.description: Verbatim source text supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: supporting_chunk_id
core_fields.description: Evidence chunk identifier supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: statistical_count_type
core_fields.description: Count semantics such as cumulative, annual, newly_reported, or point-in-time.

core_fields.name: reporting_period
core_fields.description: Reporting period or temporal aggregation window stated by the source.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about COVID-19.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

count_semantics_notes: Separate cases, deaths, hospitalizations, test positivity, and wastewater signals — do not aggregate across metric types.
Dashboard reporting periods may be weekly, monthly, or cumulative; always record the exact reporting period covered.
Distinguish between new/incident counts and cumulative totals; prefer incident counts for the 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07 window.
New York State and New York City may report separately; record subnational_location and locality precisely to avoid double-counting.
As of early 2024, many jurisdictions had reduced COVID-19 reporting frequency; weekly aggregates may be the finest granularity available.
Test positivity rate is a surveillance signal, not a case count — do not substitute for cases_confirmed.
Wastewater surveillance data is a proxy signal — record separately and do not conflate with clinical case counts.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix COVID-19-only counts with all-respiratory-virus counts (e.g., combined flu/RSV/COVID dashboards).
Do not mix test positivity rate with case counts.
New York State totals may or may not include New York City; verify inclusion/exclusion explicitly.
Cumulative counts must not be reported as incident counts for the target week.
CDC national aggregates must not be substituted for New York-specific figures.
Some 2024 dashboards report hospitalizations as 7-day averages rather than weekly totals — note the metric definition.
Probable and suspected case definitions vary by jurisdiction and reporting period; record case classification as reported.

core_fields.name: cases_suspected
core_fields.description: Source-defined suspected human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_unspecified
core_fields.description: Human cases where confirmation status is not clearly stated.

core_fields.name: deaths
core_fields.description: Deaths attributed to the reported disease event or surveillance period.

core_fields.name: case_definition
core_fields.description: Case definition or count label used by the source.

core_fields.name: source_id
core_fields.description: Workflow source identifier when available.

core_fields.name: source_url

core_fields.name: source_type
core_fields.description: Source category used by the data collection workflow.

core_fields.name: evidence_quote
core_fields.description: Verbatim source text supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: supporting_chunk_id
core_fields.description: Evidence chunk identifier supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: statistical_count_type
core_fields.description: Count semantics such as cumulative, annual, newly_reported, or point-in-time.

core_fields.name: reporting_period
core_fields.description: Reporting period or temporal aggregation window stated by the source.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about COVID-19.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

WHO situation reports and PAHO regional updates may include US or New York COVID-19 data for the target window, providing an independent validation layer against official agency figures.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints covering New York COVID-19 epidemiology in early 2024 (e.g., JN.1 variant wave) provide case definitions, count semantics, and epidemiological context for interpreting extracted records.

Reputable news outlets (e.g., New York Times, AP, local NY outlets) and situation reports may cite official New York COVID-19 figures for the first week of January 2024, providing collection support and pointers to official sources.

This query directly targets data.cdc.gov for New York weekly data with the 'week ending' phrase and January 2024 time anchor, which matches the dataset's column naming convention. This is the most direct path to confirmed numeric case and death counts for New York for the target week.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC Socrata open data dataset page or API endpoint for weekly COVID-19 cases and deaths by state, with a New York row for week ending January 6 or January 7, 2024
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: Federal government domain (data.cdc.gov), CDC authorship, Socrata structured dataset with state-level weekly rows

iterative_search_queries.query: site:health.data.ny.gov COVID-19 hospitalizations cases January 2024 weekly
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: The NYSDOH open data portal (health.data.ny.gov) is a distinct domain from coronavirus.health.ny.gov and hosts downloadable machine-readable datasets including the COVID-19 hospitalization time-series referenced in the NYSDOH hospitalization dashboard snippet ('Historical daily data can be accessed via this Open Data COVID-19 hospitalizations file'). This query directly targets that portal for January 2024 data, which should yield the specific hospitalization counts for the target week.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: NYSDOH open data portal dataset page for COVID-19 hospitalizations or cases with daily/weekly rows covering January 2024, filterable by date
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: New York State government domain (health.data.ny.gov), NYSDOH authorship, open data portal with time-series dataset

iterative_search_queries.query: NYC DOHMH COVID-19 data "week ending" "January 2024" confirmed cases deaths hospitalizations github OR "data.cityofnewyork.us"

The data.cityofnewyork.us domain appeared in iteration 1 results. This query targets both channels with the 'week ending' phrase and January 2024 time anchor to surface the specific NYC weekly data entry for the target period.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: NYC DOHMH GitHub repository file or NYC Open Data dataset with weekly COVID-19 rows for week ending January 2024, containing confirmed/probable case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations for New York City
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: NYC DOHMH authorship, official NYC Open Data portal (data.cityofnewyork.us) or nychealth GitHub repository, weekly data with date column matching target week

count_semantics_notes: Separate cases, deaths, hospitalizations, test positivity, and wastewater signals — do not aggregate across metric types.
Dashboard reporting periods may be weekly, monthly, or cumulative; always record the exact reporting period covered.
Distinguish between new/incident counts and cumulative totals; prefer incident counts for the 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07 window.
New York State and New York City may report separately; record subnational_location and locality precisely to avoid double-counting.
As of early 2024, many jurisdictions had reduced COVID-19 reporting frequency; weekly aggregates may be the finest granularity available.
Test positivity rate is a surveillance signal, not a case count — do not substitute for cases_confirmed.
Wastewater surveillance data is a proxy signal — record separately and do not conflate with clinical case counts.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix COVID-19-only counts with all-respiratory-virus counts (e.g., combined flu/RSV/COVID dashboards).
Do not mix test positivity rate with case counts.
New York State totals may or may not include New York City; verify inclusion/exclusion explicitly.
Cumulative counts must not be reported as incident counts for the target week.
CDC national aggregates must not be substituted for New York-specific figures.
Some 2024 dashboards report hospitalizations as 7-day averages rather than weekly totals — note the metric definition.
Probable and suspected case definitions vary by jurisdiction and reporting period; record case classification as reported.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about COVID-19.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify primary official reporting sources for COVID-19 human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in New York (state and city) during 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: NYSDOH and NYC DOHMH are the authoritative subnational agencies publishing weekly COVID-19 surveillance data for New York. Their dashboards, weekly reports, and data downloads are the highest-priority extractable collection sources for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC state-level COVID-19 surveillance data covering New York for the week of 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC publishes state-level COVID-19 case, death, and hospitalization data through its COVID Data Tracker and associated datasets, which may include New York-specific breakdowns for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify HHS Protect or HealthData.gov structured datasets reporting New York COVID-19 hospitalizations for the target week.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: HHS Protect publishes hospital-level and state-level COVID-19 hospitalization data as open structured datasets, which may contain New York records for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent summary or structured sources (e.g., WHO situation reports, PAHO, Our World in Data) to compare against collected New York COVID-19 records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Held-back or independent aggregator sources support masked validation of case and death counts without contaminating the primary collection pipeline.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify structured open-data portals (e.g., NYC Open Data, New York State Open Data) with COVID-19 datasets covering the target window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Open data portals may publish machine-readable COVID-19 datasets that can serve as independent validation against official agency narrative reports.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify context sources clarifying COVID-19 case definitions, count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), and reporting period conventions used by New York agencies in early 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definition and count-type context is essential for correct normalization of extracted records, especially given the transition in COVID-19 reporting frameworks in 2023–2024.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints reporting New York COVID-19 epidemiology for January 2024 or the surrounding period.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources may provide case definitions, variant context (JN.1 wave), and epidemiological framing useful for interpreting extracted counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation reports covering New York COVID-19 case and death trends during the first week of January 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may surface early outbreak signals, reference official figures, or link to official dashboards not yet identified through direct agency searches.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources with ambiguous geographic scope (e.g., national aggregates without NY breakdown), unclear count semantics, or validation leakage risk for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources that cannot be clearly assigned to collection or validation, or whose counts cannot be unambiguously attributed to the target window and location, must be flagged before entering extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: NYSDOH, NYC DOHMH, and CDC are the primary authoritative agencies publishing COVID-19 case, death, and hospitalization surveillance data for New York. NYSDOH publishes weekly COVID-19 reports; NYC DOHMH publishes city-level data; CDC COVID Data Tracker publishes state-level breakdowns. These are the highest-priority extractable collection sources for the 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07 window.

Structured open-data portals such as NYC Open Data, New York State Open Data, HealthData.gov, and HHS Protect publish machine-readable COVID-19 datasets that can serve as independent validation sources. These datasets may include daily or weekly case, death, and hospitalization counts for New York.
WHO situation reports and PAHO regional updates may include US or New York COVID-19 data for the target window, providing an independent validation layer against official agency figures.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints covering New York COVID-19 epidemiology in early 2024 (e.g., JN.1 variant wave) provide case definitions, count semantics, and epidemiological context for interpreting extracted records.

Reputable news outlets (e.g., New York Times, AP, local NY outlets) and situation reports may cite official New York COVID-19 figures for the first week of January 2024, providing collection support and pointers to official sources.

count_semantics_notes: Separate cases, deaths, hospitalizations, test positivity, and wastewater signals — do not aggregate across metric types.
Dashboard reporting periods may be weekly, monthly, or cumulative; always record the exact reporting period covered.
Distinguish between new/incident counts and cumulative totals; prefer incident counts for the 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07 window.
New York State and New York City may report separately; record subnational_location and locality precisely to avoid double-counting.
As of early 2024, many jurisdictions had reduced COVID-19 reporting frequency; weekly aggregates may be the finest granularity available.
Test positivity rate is a surveillance signal, not a case count — do not substitute for cases_confirmed.
Wastewater surveillance data is a proxy signal — record separately and do not conflate with clinical case counts.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix COVID-19-only counts with all-respiratory-virus counts (e.g., combined flu/RSV/COVID dashboards).
Do not mix test positivity rate with case counts.
New York State totals may or may not include New York City; verify inclusion/exclusion explicitly.
Cumulative counts must not be reported as incident counts for the target week.
CDC national aggregates must not be substituted for New York-specific figures.
Some 2024 dashboards report hospitalizations as 7-day averages rather than weekly totals — note the metric definition.
Probable and suspected case definitions vary by jurisdiction and reporting period; record case classification as reported.
exclusion_terms: generic respiratory virus without COVID-19 data
flu and RSV combined without COVID-19 breakdown

collection_schema.description: Disease-aware generic public-health collection schema generated for COVID-19 from structured task input and disease intelligence.

core_fields.name: disease
core_fields.description: Standard disease name for the requested task.

core_fields.name: virus_or_syndrome
core_fields.description: Specific pathogen, syndrome, or disease subtype if stated by the source.

core_fields.name: country
core_fields.description: Country where the human cases, deaths, outbreak, or surveillance data occurred.

core_fields.name: subnational_location
core_fields.description: State, province, city, county, district, hospital, or other subnational location as stated.

core_fields.name: date_reported
core_fields.description: Date when the data were reported or published; preserve partial dates when needed.

core_fields.name: event_start_date
core_fields.description: Start date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: event_end_date
core_fields.description: End date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: cases_confirmed
core_fields.description: Laboratory-confirmed or source-defined confirmed human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_probable
core_fields.description: Source-defined probable human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_suspected
core_fields.description: Source-defined suspected human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_unspecified
core_fields.description: Human cases where confirmation status is not clearly stated.

core_fields.name: deaths
core_fields.description: Deaths attributed to the reported disease event or surveillance period.

core_fields.name: case_definition
core_fields.description: Case definition or count label used by the source.

core_fields.name: source_id
core_fields.description: Workflow source identifier when available.

core_fields.name: source_url
core_fields.description: URL of the source from which the record was extracted.

core_fields.name: source_type
core_fields.description: Source category used by the data collection workflow.

core_fields.name: evidence_quote
core_fields.description: Verbatim source text supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: supporting_chunk_id
core_fields.description: Evidence chunk identifier supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: statistical_count_type
core_fields.description: Count semantics such as cumulative, annual, newly_reported, or point-in-time.

core_fields.name: reporting_period
core_fields.description: Reporting period or temporal aggregation window stated by the source.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about COVID-19.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify primary official reporting sources for COVID-19 human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in New York (state and city) during 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: NYSDOH and NYC DOHMH are the authoritative subnational agencies publishing weekly COVID-19 surveillance data for New York. Their dashboards, weekly reports, and data downloads are the highest-priority extractable collection sources for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC state-level COVID-19 surveillance data covering New York for the week of 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC publishes state-level COVID-19 case, death, and hospitalization data through its COVID Data Tracker and associated datasets, which may include New York-specific breakdowns for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify HHS Protect or HealthData.gov structured datasets reporting New York COVID-19 hospitalizations for the target week.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: HHS Protect publishes hospital-level and state-level COVID-19 hospitalization data as open structured datasets, which may contain New York records for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent summary or structured sources (e.g., WHO situation reports, PAHO, Our World in Data) to compare against collected New York COVID-19 records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Held-back or independent aggregator sources support masked validation of case and death counts without contaminating the primary collection pipeline.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify structured open-data portals (e.g., NYC Open Data, New York State Open Data) with COVID-19 datasets covering the target window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Open data portals may publish machine-readable COVID-19 datasets that can serve as independent validation against official agency narrative reports.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify context sources clarifying COVID-19 case definitions, count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), and reporting period conventions used by New York agencies in early 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definition and count-type context is essential for correct normalization of extracted records, especially given the transition in COVID-19 reporting frameworks in 2023–2024.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints reporting New York COVID-19 epidemiology for January 2024 or the surrounding period.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources may provide case definitions, variant context (JN.1 wave), and epidemiological framing useful for interpreting extracted counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation reports covering New York COVID-19 case and death trends during the first week of January 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may surface early outbreak signals, reference official figures, or link to official dashboards not yet identified through direct agency searches.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources with ambiguous geographic scope (e.g., national aggregates without NY breakdown), unclear count semantics, or validation leakage risk for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources that cannot be clearly assigned to collection or validation, or whose counts cannot be unambiguously attributed to the target window and location, must be flagged before entering extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: NYSDOH, NYC DOHMH, and CDC are the primary authoritative agencies publishing COVID-19 case, death, and hospitalization surveillance data for New York. NYSDOH publishes weekly COVID-19 reports; NYC DOHMH publishes city-level data; CDC COVID Data Tracker publishes state-level breakdowns. These are the highest-priority extractable collection sources for the 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07 window.

Structured open-data portals such as NYC Open Data, New York State Open Data, HealthData.gov, and HHS Protect publish machine-readable COVID-19 datasets that can serve as independent validation sources. These datasets may include daily or weekly case, death, and hospitalization counts for New York.
WHO situation reports and PAHO regional updates may include US or New York COVID-19 data for the target window, providing an independent validation layer against official agency figures.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints covering New York COVID-19 epidemiology in early 2024 (e.g., JN.1 variant wave) provide case definitions, count semantics, and epidemiological context for interpreting extracted records.

Reputable news outlets (e.g., New York Times, AP, local NY outlets) and situation reports may cite official New York COVID-19 figures for the first week of January 2024, providing collection support and pointers to official sources.

count_semantics_notes: Separate cases, deaths, hospitalizations, test positivity, and wastewater signals — do not aggregate across metric types.

Distinguish between new/incident counts and cumulative totals; prefer incident counts for the 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07 window.
New York State and New York City may report separately; record subnational_location and locality precisely to avoid double-counting.
As of early 2024, many jurisdictions had reduced COVID-19 reporting frequency; weekly aggregates may be the finest granularity available.
Test positivity rate is a surveillance signal, not a case count — do not substitute for cases_confirmed.
Wastewater surveillance data is a proxy signal — record separately and do not conflate with clinical case counts.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix COVID-19-only counts with all-respiratory-virus counts (e.g., combined flu/RSV/COVID dashboards).
Do not mix test positivity rate with case counts.
New York State totals may or may not include New York City; verify inclusion/exclusion explicitly.
Cumulative counts must not be reported as incident counts for the target week.
CDC national aggregates must not be substituted for New York-specific figures.

Probable and suspected case definitions vary by jurisdiction and reporting period; record case classification as reported.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about COVID-19.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify primary official reporting sources for COVID-19 human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in New York (state and city) during 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: NYSDOH and NYC DOHMH are the authoritative subnational agencies publishing weekly COVID-19 surveillance data for New York. Their dashboards, weekly reports, and data downloads are the highest-priority extractable collection sources for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC state-level COVID-19 surveillance data covering New York for the week of 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC publishes state-level COVID-19 case, death, and hospitalization data through its COVID Data Tracker and associated datasets, which may include New York-specific breakdowns for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify HHS Protect or HealthData.gov structured datasets reporting New York COVID-19 hospitalizations for the target week.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: HHS Protect publishes hospital-level and state-level COVID-19 hospitalization data as open structured datasets, which may contain New York records for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent summary or structured sources (e.g., WHO situation reports, PAHO, Our World in Data) to compare against collected New York COVID-19 records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Held-back or independent aggregator sources support masked validation of case and death counts without contaminating the primary collection pipeline.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify structured open-data portals (e.g., NYC Open Data, New York State Open Data) with COVID-19 datasets covering the target window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Open data portals may publish machine-readable COVID-19 datasets that can serve as independent validation against official agency narrative reports.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify context sources clarifying COVID-19 case definitions, count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), and reporting period conventions used by New York agencies in early 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definition and count-type context is essential for correct normalization of extracted records, especially given the transition in COVID-19 reporting frameworks in 2023–2024.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints reporting New York COVID-19 epidemiology for January 2024 or the surrounding period.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources may provide case definitions, variant context (JN.1 wave), and epidemiological framing useful for interpreting extracted counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation reports covering New York COVID-19 case and death trends during the first week of January 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may surface early outbreak signals, reference official figures, or link to official dashboards not yet identified through direct agency searches.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources with ambiguous geographic scope (e.g., national aggregates without NY breakdown), unclear count semantics, or validation leakage risk for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources that cannot be clearly assigned to collection or validation, or whose counts cannot be unambiguously attributed to the target window and location, must be flagged before entering extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: NYSDOH, NYC DOHMH, and CDC are the primary authoritative agencies publishing COVID-19 case, death, and hospitalization surveillance data for New York. NYSDOH publishes weekly COVID-19 reports; NYC DOHMH publishes city-level data; CDC COVID Data Tracker publishes state-level breakdowns. These are the highest-priority extractable collection sources for the 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07 window.

Structured open-data portals such as NYC Open Data, New York State Open Data, HealthData.gov, and HHS Protect publish machine-readable COVID-19 datasets that can serve as independent validation sources. These datasets may include daily or weekly case, death, and hospitalization counts for New York.
WHO situation reports and PAHO regional updates may include US or New York COVID-19 data for the target window, providing an independent validation layer against official agency figures.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints covering New York COVID-19 epidemiology in early 2024 (e.g., JN.1 variant wave) provide case definitions, count semantics, and epidemiological context for interpreting extracted records.

Reputable news outlets (e.g., New York Times, AP, local NY outlets) and situation reports may cite official New York COVID-19 figures for the first week of January 2024, providing collection support and pointers to official sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify primary official reporting sources for COVID-19 human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in New York (state and city) during 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: NYSDOH and NYC DOHMH are the authoritative subnational agencies publishing weekly COVID-19 surveillance data for New York. Their dashboards, weekly reports, and data downloads are the highest-priority extractable collection sources for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC state-level COVID-19 surveillance data covering New York for the week of 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC publishes state-level COVID-19 case, death, and hospitalization data through its COVID Data Tracker and associated datasets, which may include New York-specific breakdowns for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify HHS Protect or HealthData.gov structured datasets reporting New York COVID-19 hospitalizations for the target week.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: HHS Protect publishes hospital-level and state-level COVID-19 hospitalization data as open structured datasets, which may contain New York records for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent summary or structured sources (e.g., WHO situation reports, PAHO, Our World in Data) to compare against collected New York COVID-19 records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Held-back or independent aggregator sources support masked validation of case and death counts without contaminating the primary collection pipeline.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify structured open-data portals (e.g., NYC Open Data, New York State Open Data) with COVID-19 datasets covering the target window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Open data portals may publish machine-readable COVID-19 datasets that can serve as independent validation against official agency narrative reports.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify context sources clarifying COVID-19 case definitions, count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), and reporting period conventions used by New York agencies in early 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definition and count-type context is essential for correct normalization of extracted records, especially given the transition in COVID-19 reporting frameworks in 2023–2024.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints reporting New York COVID-19 epidemiology for January 2024 or the surrounding period.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources may provide case definitions, variant context (JN.1 wave), and epidemiological framing useful for interpreting extracted counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation reports covering New York COVID-19 case and death trends during the first week of January 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may surface early outbreak signals, reference official figures, or link to official dashboards not yet identified through direct agency searches.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources with ambiguous geographic scope (e.g., national aggregates without NY breakdown), unclear count semantics, or validation leakage risk for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources that cannot be clearly assigned to collection or validation, or whose counts cannot be unambiguously attributed to the target window and location, must be flagged before entering extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: NYSDOH, NYC DOHMH, and CDC are the primary authoritative agencies publishing COVID-19 case, death, and hospitalization surveillance data for New York. NYSDOH publishes weekly COVID-19 reports; NYC DOHMH publishes city-level data; CDC COVID Data Tracker publishes state-level breakdowns. These are the highest-priority extractable collection sources for the 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07 window.

Structured open-data portals such as NYC Open Data, New York State Open Data, HealthData.gov, and HHS Protect publish machine-readable COVID-19 datasets that can serve as independent validation sources. These datasets may include daily or weekly case, death, and hospitalization counts for New York.
WHO situation reports and PAHO regional updates may include US or New York COVID-19 data for the target window, providing an independent validation layer against official agency figures.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints covering New York COVID-19 epidemiology in early 2024 (e.g., JN.1 variant wave) provide case definitions, count semantics, and epidemiological context for interpreting extracted records.

Reputable news outlets (e.g., New York Times, AP, local NY outlets) and situation reports may cite official New York COVID-19 figures for the first week of January 2024, providing collection support and pointers to official sources.

count_semantics_notes: Separate cases, deaths, hospitalizations, test positivity, and wastewater signals — do not aggregate across metric types.

Wastewater surveillance data is a proxy signal — record separately and do not conflate with clinical case counts.

Do not mix test positivity rate with case counts.

Cumulative counts must not be reported as incident counts for the target week.
CDC national aggregates must not be substituted for New York-specific figures.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about COVID-19.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify primary official reporting sources for COVID-19 human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in New York (state and city) during 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: NYSDOH and NYC DOHMH are the authoritative subnational agencies publishing weekly COVID-19 surveillance data for New York. Their dashboards, weekly reports, and data downloads are the highest-priority extractable collection sources for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC state-level COVID-19 surveillance data covering New York for the week of 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC publishes state-level COVID-19 case, death, and hospitalization data through its COVID Data Tracker and associated datasets, which may include New York-specific breakdowns for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify HHS Protect or HealthData.gov structured datasets reporting New York COVID-19 hospitalizations for the target week.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: HHS Protect publishes hospital-level and state-level COVID-19 hospitalization data as open structured datasets, which may contain New York records for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent summary or structured sources (e.g., WHO situation reports, PAHO, Our World in Data) to compare against collected New York COVID-19 records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Held-back or independent aggregator sources support masked validation of case and death counts without contaminating the primary collection pipeline.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify structured open-data portals (e.g., NYC Open Data, New York State Open Data) with COVID-19 datasets covering the target window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Open data portals may publish machine-readable COVID-19 datasets that can serve as independent validation against official agency narrative reports.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify context sources clarifying COVID-19 case definitions, count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), and reporting period conventions used by New York agencies in early 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definition and count-type context is essential for correct normalization of extracted records, especially given the transition in COVID-19 reporting frameworks in 2023–2024.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints reporting New York COVID-19 epidemiology for January 2024 or the surrounding period.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources may provide case definitions, variant context (JN.1 wave), and epidemiological framing useful for interpreting extracted counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation reports covering New York COVID-19 case and death trends during the first week of January 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may surface early outbreak signals, reference official figures, or link to official dashboards not yet identified through direct agency searches.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources with ambiguous geographic scope (e.g., national aggregates without NY breakdown), unclear count semantics, or validation leakage risk for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources that cannot be clearly assigned to collection or validation, or whose counts cannot be unambiguously attributed to the target window and location, must be flagged before entering extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: NYSDOH, NYC DOHMH, and CDC are the primary authoritative agencies publishing COVID-19 case, death, and hospitalization surveillance data for New York. NYSDOH publishes weekly COVID-19 reports; NYC DOHMH publishes city-level data; CDC COVID Data Tracker publishes state-level breakdowns. These are the highest-priority extractable collection sources for the 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07 window.

Structured open-data portals such as NYC Open Data, New York State Open Data, HealthData.gov, and HHS Protect publish machine-readable COVID-19 datasets that can serve as independent validation sources. These datasets may include daily or weekly case, death, and hospitalization counts for New York.
WHO situation reports and PAHO regional updates may include US or New York COVID-19 data for the target window, providing an independent validation layer against official agency figures.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints covering New York COVID-19 epidemiology in early 2024 (e.g., JN.1 variant wave) provide case definitions, count semantics, and epidemiological context for interpreting extracted records.

Reputable news outlets (e.g., New York Times, AP, local NY outlets) and situation reports may cite official New York COVID-19 figures for the first week of January 2024, providing collection support and pointers to official sources.

collection_spec.data_focus: human COVID-19 case, outbreak, and surveillance data

official_source_terms: New York State Department of Health
likely_reporting_agencies: New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH)
New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (NYC DOHMH)
count_semantics_notes: Separate cases, deaths, hospitalizations, test positivity, and wastewater signals — do not aggregate across metric types.
Dashboard reporting periods may be weekly, monthly, or cumulative; always record the exact reporting period covered.
Distinguish between new/incident counts and cumulative totals; prefer incident counts for the 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07 window.
New York State and New York City may report separately; record subnational_location and locality precisely to avoid double-counting.
As of early 2024, many jurisdictions had reduced COVID-19 reporting frequency; weekly aggregates may be the finest granularity available.
Test positivity rate is a surveillance signal, not a case count — do not substitute for cases_confirmed.
Wastewater surveillance data is a proxy signal — record separately and do not conflate with clinical case counts.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix COVID-19-only counts with all-respiratory-virus counts (e.g., combined flu/RSV/COVID dashboards).
Do not mix test positivity rate with case counts.
New York State totals may or may not include New York City; verify inclusion/exclusion explicitly.
Cumulative counts must not be reported as incident counts for the target week.
CDC national aggregates must not be substituted for New York-specific figures.
Some 2024 dashboards report hospitalizations as 7-day averages rather than weekly totals — note the metric definition.
Probable and suspected case definitions vary by jurisdiction and reporting period; record case classification as reported.
exclusion_terms: generic respiratory virus without COVID-19 data
flu and RSV combined without COVID-19 breakdown
suggested_query_templates: "New York State Department of Health" COVID-19 cases January 2024
warnings: As of early 2024, many U.S. state and local COVID-19 dashboards had reduced reporting frequency or granularity; weekly incident data for 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07 may require aggregation from multiple sub-weekly reports or may only be available as a weekly summary.
New York State and New York City maintain separate reporting systems; both must be queried independently to achieve full geographic coverage, and double-counting must be avoided when combining.
CDC transitioned COVID-19 data reporting in 2023–2024; verify which CDC datasets remain active and cover the target time window.

collection_schema.description: Disease-aware generic public-health collection schema generated for COVID-19 from structured task input and disease intelligence.

core_fields.name: disease
core_fields.description: Standard disease name for the requested task.

core_fields.name: virus_or_syndrome
core_fields.description: Specific pathogen, syndrome, or disease subtype if stated by the source.

core_fields.name: country
core_fields.description: Country where the human cases, deaths, outbreak, or surveillance data occurred.

core_fields.name: subnational_location
core_fields.description: State, province, city, county, district, hospital, or other subnational location as stated.

core_fields.name: date_reported
core_fields.description: Date when the data were reported or published; preserve partial dates when needed.

core_fields.name: event_start_date
core_fields.description: Start date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: event_end_date
core_fields.description: End date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: cases_confirmed
core_fields.description: Laboratory-confirmed or source-defined confirmed human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_probable
core_fields.description: Source-defined probable human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_suspected
core_fields.description: Source-defined suspected human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_unspecified
core_fields.description: Human cases where confirmation status is not clearly stated.

core_fields.name: deaths
core_fields.description: Deaths attributed to the reported disease event or surveillance period.

core_fields.name: case_definition
core_fields.description: Case definition or count label used by the source.

core_fields.name: source_id
core_fields.description: Workflow source identifier when available.

core_fields.name: source_url
core_fields.description: URL of the source from which the record was extracted.

core_fields.name: source_type
core_fields.description: Source category used by the data collection workflow.

core_fields.name: evidence_quote
core_fields.description: Verbatim source text supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: supporting_chunk_id
core_fields.description: Evidence chunk identifier supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: statistical_count_type
core_fields.description: Count semantics such as cumulative, annual, newly_reported, or point-in-time.

core_fields.name: reporting_period
core_fields.description: Reporting period or temporal aggregation window stated by the source.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about COVID-19.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.

source_discovery_objectives.rationale: NYSDOH and NYC DOHMH are the authoritative subnational agencies publishing weekly COVID-19 surveillance data for New York. Their dashboards, weekly reports, and data downloads are the highest-priority extractable collection sources for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC state-level COVID-19 surveillance data covering New York for the week of 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC publishes state-level COVID-19 case, death, and hospitalization data through its COVID Data Tracker and associated datasets, which may include New York-specific breakdowns for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify HHS Protect or HealthData.gov structured datasets reporting New York COVID-19 hospitalizations for the target week.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: HHS Protect publishes hospital-level and state-level COVID-19 hospitalization data as open structured datasets, which may contain New York records for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent summary or structured sources (e.g., WHO situation reports, PAHO, Our World in Data) to compare against collected New York COVID-19 records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Held-back or independent aggregator sources support masked validation of case and death counts without contaminating the primary collection pipeline.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify structured open-data portals (e.g., NYC Open Data, New York State Open Data) with COVID-19 datasets covering the target window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Open data portals may publish machine-readable COVID-19 datasets that can serve as independent validation against official agency narrative reports.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify context sources clarifying COVID-19 case definitions, count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), and reporting period conventions used by New York agencies in early 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definition and count-type context is essential for correct normalization of extracted records, especially given the transition in COVID-19 reporting frameworks in 2023–2024.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints reporting New York COVID-19 epidemiology for January 2024 or the surrounding period.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources may provide case definitions, variant context (JN.1 wave), and epidemiological framing useful for interpreting extracted counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation reports covering New York COVID-19 case and death trends during the first week of January 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may surface early outbreak signals, reference official figures, or link to official dashboards not yet identified through direct agency searches.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources with ambiguous geographic scope (e.g., national aggregates without NY breakdown), unclear count semantics, or validation leakage risk for human review.

Reputable news outlets (e.g., New York Times, AP, local NY outlets) and situation reports may cite official New York COVID-19 figures for the first week of January 2024, providing collection support and pointers to official sources.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about COVID-19.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify primary official reporting sources for COVID-19 human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in New York (state and city) during 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: NYSDOH and NYC DOHMH are the authoritative subnational agencies publishing weekly COVID-19 surveillance data for New York. Their dashboards, weekly reports, and data downloads are the highest-priority extractable collection sources for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC state-level COVID-19 surveillance data covering New York for the week of 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC publishes state-level COVID-19 case, death, and hospitalization data through its COVID Data Tracker and associated datasets, which may include New York-specific breakdowns for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify HHS Protect or HealthData.gov structured datasets reporting New York COVID-19 hospitalizations for the target week.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: HHS Protect publishes hospital-level and state-level COVID-19 hospitalization data as open structured datasets, which may contain New York records for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent summary or structured sources (e.g., WHO situation reports, PAHO, Our World in Data) to compare against collected New York COVID-19 records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Held-back or independent aggregator sources support masked validation of case and death counts without contaminating the primary collection pipeline.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify structured open-data portals (e.g., NYC Open Data, New York State Open Data) with COVID-19 datasets covering the target window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Open data portals may publish machine-readable COVID-19 datasets that can serve as independent validation against official agency narrative reports.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify context sources clarifying COVID-19 case definitions, count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), and reporting period conventions used by New York agencies in early 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definition and count-type context is essential for correct normalization of extracted records, especially given the transition in COVID-19 reporting frameworks in 2023–2024.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints reporting New York COVID-19 epidemiology for January 2024 or the surrounding period.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources may provide case definitions, variant context (JN.1 wave), and epidemiological framing useful for interpreting extracted counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation reports covering New York COVID-19 case and death trends during the first week of January 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may surface early outbreak signals, reference official figures, or link to official dashboards not yet identified through direct agency searches.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources with ambiguous geographic scope (e.g., national aggregates without NY breakdown), unclear count semantics, or validation leakage risk for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources that cannot be clearly assigned to collection or validation, or whose counts cannot be unambiguously attributed to the target window and location, must be flagged before entering extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: NYSDOH, NYC DOHMH, and CDC are the primary authoritative agencies publishing COVID-19 case, death, and hospitalization surveillance data for New York. NYSDOH publishes weekly COVID-19 reports; NYC DOHMH publishes city-level data; CDC COVID Data Tracker publishes state-level breakdowns. These are the highest-priority extractable collection sources for the 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07 window.

Structured open-data portals such as NYC Open Data, New York State Open Data, HealthData.gov, and HHS Protect publish machine-readable COVID-19 datasets that can serve as independent validation sources. These datasets may include daily or weekly case, death, and hospitalization counts for New York.
WHO situation reports and PAHO regional updates may include US or New York COVID-19 data for the target window, providing an independent validation layer against official agency figures.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints covering New York COVID-19 epidemiology in early 2024 (e.g., JN.1 variant wave) provide case definitions, count semantics, and epidemiological context for interpreting extracted records.

Reputable news outlets (e.g., New York Times, AP, local NY outlets) and situation reports may cite official New York COVID-19 figures for the first week of January 2024, providing collection support and pointers to official sources.

count_semantics_notes: Separate cases, deaths, hospitalizations, test positivity, and wastewater signals — do not aggregate across metric types.

Wastewater surveillance data is a proxy signal — record separately and do not conflate with clinical case counts.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about COVID-19.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify primary official reporting sources for COVID-19 human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in New York (state and city) during 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: NYSDOH and NYC DOHMH are the authoritative subnational agencies publishing weekly COVID-19 surveillance data for New York. Their dashboards, weekly reports, and data downloads are the highest-priority extractable collection sources for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC state-level COVID-19 surveillance data covering New York for the week of 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC publishes state-level COVID-19 case, death, and hospitalization data through its COVID Data Tracker and associated datasets, which may include New York-specific breakdowns for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify HHS Protect or HealthData.gov structured datasets reporting New York COVID-19 hospitalizations for the target week.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: HHS Protect publishes hospital-level and state-level COVID-19 hospitalization data as open structured datasets, which may contain New York records for the target window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent summary or structured sources (e.g., WHO situation reports, PAHO, Our World in Data) to compare against collected New York COVID-19 records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Held-back or independent aggregator sources support masked validation of case and death counts without contaminating the primary collection pipeline.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify structured open-data portals (e.g., NYC Open Data, New York State Open Data) with COVID-19 datasets covering the target window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Open data portals may publish machine-readable COVID-19 datasets that can serve as independent validation against official agency narrative reports.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify context sources clarifying COVID-19 case definitions, count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), and reporting period conventions used by New York agencies in early 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definition and count-type context is essential for correct normalization of extracted records, especially given the transition in COVID-19 reporting frameworks in 2023–2024.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints reporting New York COVID-19 epidemiology for January 2024 or the surrounding period.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources may provide case definitions, variant context (JN.1 wave), and epidemiological framing useful for interpreting extracted counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation reports covering New York COVID-19 case and death trends during the first week of January 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may surface early outbreak signals, reference official figures, or link to official dashboards not yet identified through direct agency searches.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources with ambiguous geographic scope (e.g., national aggregates without NY breakdown), unclear count semantics, or validation leakage risk for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources that cannot be clearly assigned to collection or validation, or whose counts cannot be unambiguously attributed to the target window and location, must be flagged before entering extraction.

WHO situation reports and PAHO regional updates may include US or New York COVID-19 data for the target window, providing an independent validation layer against official agency figures.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints covering New York COVID-19 epidemiology in early 2024 (e.g., JN.1 variant wave) provide case definitions, count semantics, and epidemiological context for interpreting extracted records.

Reputable news outlets (e.g., New York Times, AP, local NY outlets) and situation reports may cite official New York COVID-19 figures for the first week of January 2024, providing collection support and pointers to official sources.

count_semantics_notes: Separate cases, deaths, hospitalizations, test positivity, and wastewater signals — do not aggregate across metric types.
Dashboard reporting periods may be weekly, monthly, or cumulative; always record the exact reporting period covered.
Distinguish between new/incident counts and cumulative totals; prefer incident counts for the 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07 window.
New York State and New York City may report separately; record subnational_location and locality precisely to avoid double-counting.
As of early 2024, many jurisdictions had reduced COVID-19 reporting frequency; weekly aggregates may be the finest granularity available.
Test positivity rate is a surveillance signal, not a case count — do not substitute for cases_confirmed.
Wastewater surveillance data is a proxy signal — record separately and do not conflate with clinical case counts.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix COVID-19-only counts with all-respiratory-virus counts (e.g., combined flu/RSV/COVID dashboards).
Do not mix test positivity rate with case counts.
New York State totals may or may not include New York City; verify inclusion/exclusion explicitly.
Cumulative counts must not be reported as incident counts for the target week.
CDC national aggregates must not be substituted for New York-specific figures.
Some 2024 dashboards report hospitalizations as 7-day averages rather than weekly totals — note the metric definition.
Probable and suspected case definitions vary by jurisdiction and reporting period; record case classification as reported.

flu and RSV combined without COVID-19 breakdown

warnings: As of early 2024, many U.S. state and local COVID-19 dashboards had reduced reporting frequency or granularity; weekly incident data for 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07 may require aggregation from multiple sub-weekly reports or may only be available as a weekly summary.
New York State and New York City maintain separate reporting systems; both must be queried independently to achieve full geographic coverage, and double-counting must be avoided when combining.
CDC transitioned COVID-19 data reporting in 2023–2024; verify which CDC datasets remain active and cover the target time window.

collection_schema.description: Disease-aware generic public-health collection schema generated for COVID-19 from structured task input and disease intelligence.

core_fields.name: disease
core_fields.description: Standard disease name for the requested task.

core_fields.name: virus_or_syndrome
core_fields.description: Specific pathogen, syndrome, or disease subtype if stated by the source.

core_fields.name: country
core_fields.description: Country where the human cases, deaths, outbreak, or surveillance data occurred.

core_fields.name: subnational_location
core_fields.description: State, province, city, county, district, hospital, or other subnational location as stated.

core_fields.name: date_reported
core_fields.description: Date when the data were reported or published; preserve partial dates when needed.

core_fields.name: event_start_date
core_fields.description: Start date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: event_end_date
core_fields.description: End date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: cases_confirmed
core_fields.description: Laboratory-confirmed or source-defined confirmed human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_probable
core_fields.description: Source-defined probable human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_suspected
core_fields.description: Source-defined suspected human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_unspecified
core_fields.description: Human cases where confirmation status is not clearly stated.

core_fields.name: deaths
core_fields.description: Deaths attributed to the reported disease event or surveillance period.

core_fields.name: case_definition
core_fields.description: Case definition or count label used by the source.

core_fields.name: source_id
core_fields.description: Workflow source identifier when available.

core_fields.name: source_url
core_fields.description: URL of the source from which the record was extracted.

core_fields.name: source_type
core_fields.description: Source category used by the data collection workflow.

core_fields.name: evidence_quote
core_fields.description: Verbatim source text supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: supporting_chunk_id
core_fields.description: Evidence chunk identifier supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: statistical_count_type
core_fields.description: Count semantics such as cumulative, annual, newly_reported, or point-in-time.

core_fields.name: reporting_period
core_fields.description: Reporting period or temporal aggregation window stated by the source.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about COVID-19.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

count_semantics_notes: Separate cases, deaths, hospitalizations, test positivity, and wastewater signals — do not aggregate across metric types.
Dashboard reporting periods may be weekly, monthly, or cumulative; always record the exact reporting period covered.
Distinguish between new/incident counts and cumulative totals; prefer incident counts for the 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07 window.
New York State and New York City may report separately; record subnational_location and locality precisely to avoid double-counting.
As of early 2024, many jurisdictions had reduced COVID-19 reporting frequency; weekly aggregates may be the finest granularity available.
Test positivity rate is a surveillance signal, not a case count — do not substitute for cases_confirmed.
Wastewater surveillance data is a proxy signal — record separately and do not conflate with clinical case counts.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix COVID-19-only counts with all-respiratory-virus counts (e.g., combined flu/RSV/COVID dashboards).
Do not mix test positivity rate with case counts.
New York State totals may or may not include New York City; verify inclusion/exclusion explicitly.
Cumulative counts must not be reported as incident counts for the target week.
CDC national aggregates must not be substituted for New York-specific figures.
Some 2024 dashboards report hospitalizations as 7-day averages rather than weekly totals — note the metric definition.
Probable and suspected case definitions vary by jurisdiction and reporting period; record case classification as reported.
exclusion_terms: generic respiratory virus without COVID-19 data
flu and RSV combined without COVID-19 breakdown
suggested_query_templates: "New York State Department of Health" COVID-19 cases January 2024
warnings: As of early 2024, many U.S. state and local COVID-19 dashboards had reduced reporting frequency or granularity; weekly incident data for 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-07 may require aggregation from multiple sub-weekly reports or may only be available as a weekly summary.
New York State and New York City maintain separate reporting systems; both must be queried independently to achieve full geographic coverage, and double-counting must be avoided when combining.
CDC transitioned COVID-19 data reporting in 2023–2024; verify which CDC datasets remain active and cover the target time window.

Evidence quotes must be verbatim excerpts from the source; do not paraphrase or synthesize across sources for the evidence_quote field.
If only cumulative counts are available for the target window, record as cases_unspecified with a count_semantics note; do not infer incident counts.
Wastewater and syndromic surveillance signals available for New York should be recorded as supplementary signals, not as primary case counts.
